RSCB-MC (Risk-Sensitive Contextual Bandit with Memory Control), implemented in the pythalab-codex-issue-memory artifact (commit 227bbe3, Python 3.12.3); no release version

Pattern-variant-episode issue-memory records (canonical root-cause pattern, context-specific variants with command/path/stack signatures, validated episodes); fixed 16-feature state vector (Table 1); action set of 7 actions (no memory, top1 resolution, top3 summary, high-precision retrieval, high-recall retrieval, abstain, ask feedback); risk-sensitive reward (false-positive penalty γ=4.0 > verified α=2.0 > accepted β=1.0). Offline replay, success / FP / abstention / cumulative reward (Table 6): Lexical 50.0% / 17.5% / 0.0% / -70.800; Static hybrid 50.0% / 17.5% / 0.0% / -70.800; Static+abstention 35.0% / 2.5% / 75.0% / -33.350; Epsilon-greedy 53.8% / 8.7% / 30.0% / -49.818; UCB1 55.0% / 2.5% / 50.0% / -35.865; Thompson 53.7% / 2.5% / 38.8% / -52.315; LinUCB 37.5% / 10.0% / 50.0% / -76.775; Risk-sensitive TS 60.0% / 0.0% / 37.5% / -33.700; RSCB-MC 62.5% / 0.0% / 35.0% / -31.740 (quality: works on proxy; cost: works, p95 331 µs); Oracle 67.5% / 0.0% / 50.0% / -5.900. Hard negatives (32, Table 5): Static hybrid FP 75.0%, RSCB-MC and Risk-TS 0.0% FP with 100% correct non-injection. Abstention benchmark (56): RSCB-MC correct abstention 57.1%, wrong abstention 42.9% (over-conservative). Hot-path (200 cases, Table 9): RSCB-MC 60.5% success, 0.0% FP, p95 331.466 µs; Risk-TS 60.0%, p95 411.821 µs; LinUCB p95 3567.384 µs. Ablations (Table 7): no abstention FP 17.5%, reward -87.800; no failure-family features reward -41.740. Context-budget proxy (Table 8): no memory utility 60.8% best, short hint success 74.5% / FP influence 12.0%

Tasks: seeded smoke-scale artifacts (queries, paraphrases, hard negatives, replay events). Configurations: retrieval baselines (lexical, static hybrid, static hybrid + abstention, full retriever) and bandit baselines (epsilon-greedy, UCB1, Thompson, LinUCB, risk-sensitive Thompson) vs RSCB-MC, oracle upper bound. Held constant: same artifacts and seeds, deterministic scripts. Acceptance criterion: proxy labels from replay metadata. Repetitions: 2 deterministic seeds. Human intervention: none

RSCB-MC best non-oracle replay success (62.5% vs 60.0% risk-sensitive TS, 50.0% static) with 0.0% FP (static 17.5%); 5 points below oracle; 0% FP on hard negatives vs 75% static hybrid; sub-millisecond p95 latency. No significance tests

Distinguished methods on FP and proxy success; canonical retrieval saturated (all 100%), so it did not distinguish retrieval methods. Deterministic, so repeatable. Limitations stated: smoke scale, offline replay not causal, proxy labels, reward magnitude may not alter action selection

Smoke-scale evidence only; offline replay is not a causal online evaluation; hot-path labels are proxies; context-budget and dry-run experiments are proxy tasks; single-step bandit does not model delayed multi-turn effects or memory aging; controller over-conservative (wrong abstentions); inherits stale/contradictory memory. Future: full-scale benchmark, live LLM-agent evaluation, calibration, off-policy evaluation, long-horizon modeling

Abstract and conclusion highlight 62.5% / 0.0% FP; the 'agent dry-run' experiment mentioned in limitations (p. 22) is not reported in results. Abstention text (p. 15) says RSCB-MC 'answers 0.0% of cases' and p. 19 says it 'refuses all cases', yet Table 7 gives correct abstention 5.0%; different benchmarks, not reconciled. Tables partly jumbled by pdftotext; values read in column order. No LLM or coding agent used in any experiment. Code and artifacts at github.com/PhiniteLab/codex-issue-memory. No pre-registration.
